name: American Goulash Pasta
steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion and shredded carrots, then drain.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, garlic, and italian seasoning.
Boil the penne separately until just tender, then drain.
Simmer the sauce a few minutes so it thickens, then fold in the cooked pasta.
Stir in the parmesan and portion it into containers.
head_steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion and shredded carrots, then drain.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, garlic, and italian seasoning.

findings.detail: We buy '1 stick, finely chopped (120 g)' but no step uses celery; the source (natashaskitchen) sautes it with the onion and carrot in step 2.
We buy 1 tbsp Worcestershire but no step uses it; the source stirs it in with the tomatoes and broth in step 3.
We buy 1/4 tsp sugar but no step uses it; the source seasons the vegetables with sugar in step 2.
We buy 1 tbsp olive oil but the steps brown the beef with no oil mentioned; the source browns the beef in oil in step 1.
We buy 2 tsp salt but the steps never say salt or season; the source seasons in step 2.
We buy 1/2 tsp pepper but the steps never say pepper or season.

name: Baked Turkey Kibbeh Casserole
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cover the bulgur with cold water and let it soak 20 to 30 minutes until the grains soften, then drain it and squeeze out every bit of excess water with your hands.
Set aside about a third of the ground turkey and a third of the onions for the filling, then finely mince the remaining onions for the shell.

Mix the soaked bulgur with two thirds of the ground turkey, the minced onion, the ground allspice, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper, kneading it with wet hands until it turns into a smooth, almost paste-like dough.

For the filling, heat some of the olive oil in a skillet and brown the reserved turkey with the reserved diced onion, seasoning it with more allspice, salt, and black pepper, then stir in the chopped fresh basil off the heat.
Press half the bulgur mixture into an oiled 9x13 pan in an even layer, spread the filling over it, then press the remaining bulgur mixture on top, smoothing it with wet hands.
Score the top into diamonds with a wet knife, cutting through the top layer only, then drizzle the rest of the olive oil generously over the whole surface.
Bake at 375F for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is deep golden and the edges pull away from the pan, then rest 15 minutes before portioning.
head_steps: Soak the bulgur in cold water 20 to 30 minutes, then drain and squeeze it dry.
Knead the soaked bulgur with two thirds of the ground turkey, minced onion, allspice, cumin, salt, and pepper into a smooth dough.
Brown the remaining turkey with diced onion and more allspice for the filling, then stir in the chopped basil.
Press half the bulgur dough into an oiled 9x13 pan, spread the filling over it, and press the rest of the dough on top.
Score the top into diamonds, drizzle with olive oil, bake at 375F for 40 to 45 minutes, rest 15 minutes, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 18.75 tbsp fresh mint but no step uses mint; the filling step instead says to stir in 'chopped fresh basil' (the source kibbeh uses mint/basil in the shell mixture).
Step 5 says 'stir in the chopped fresh basil off the heat' but basil is not in our list; the purchased herb is fresh mint, so the step names the wrong herb.

name: Baked Ziti with Ground Beef
ingredients: Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 28 oz dry (794 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 9.25 oz (264 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 375F. Boil the ziti in salted water until just shy of al dente, about 2 minutes under the package time. Drain.

While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground beef with the diced onion, breaking it up as it goes, until no pink remains (160F for ground beef). Add the garlic for the last minute, then stir in the marinara, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, eggs, half the Parmesan, salt, and pepper.
In two 9x13 pans, layer: a third of the meat sauce, half the pasta, half the ricotta mixture in spoonfuls, then repeat, finishing with sauce on top.
Top with the mozzarella and remaining Parmesan. Bake 25 to 30 minutes until bubbly and browned at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes before combining into your weighed pot; it holds together better and will not steam-soften in the containers.
head_steps: Boil the ziti 2 minutes shy of al dente and drain.
Brown the beef with onion and garlic until no pink remains, then stir in marinara and seasonings.
Mix ricotta with eggs and half the Parmesan.
Layer sauce, pasta, and ricotta in two 9x13 pans, then top with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake at 375F for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbly, rest 10 minutes, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 0.5 tbsp garlic powder but no step uses it; the source (realfoodwholelife) includes it in the beef seasonings in step 3.

name: Beef Birria Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stem and seed the guajillo, ancho, and arbol chiles, then toast them in a dry pan about 30 seconds a side until they smell fragrant. Do not let them blacken or the sauce turns bitter.
Cover the toasted chiles with hot water and soak 20 minutes until they are soft and pliable.
Blend the drained chiles with the diced tomatoes, onion, garlic, white vinegar, cumin, oregano, cinnamon, and cloves until completely smooth. Strain it if you want a silkier consomme.
Cut the chuck roast into large chunks, season with salt and black pepper, and sear them in the olive oil until browned.
Pour the chile sauce and the beef broth over the beef, add the bay leaves, and bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook 3.5 to 4 hours on the lowest heat that keeps it moving, until the beef falls apart when pushed.
Shred the beef and return it to the consomme, then taste and correct the salt and the vinegar.
head_steps: Toast the stemmed and seeded chiles in a dry pan, then soak them 20 minutes in hot water.
Blend the chiles with tomatoes, onion, garlic, vinegar, and spices until smooth.
Sear the seasoned chuck roast chunks in olive oil.
Add the chile sauce, beef broth, and bay leaves and simmer 3.5 to 4 hours.
Shred the beef back into the consomme and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 4.25 cups dry rice for 'Rice Bowls' but no step ever cooks or combines the rice; the steps end at shredding the beef into the consomme.

name: Beef Chili Mac
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (160 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Stir in the kidney beans, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth, chili powder, cumin, and garlic.
Simmer until the chili thickens and the flavors come together.
Boil the penne separately until just tender, then drain and fold it in.
Melt the shredded cheddar over the top before portioning into containers.
head_steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Stir in the kidney beans, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth, chili powder, cumin, and garlic.
Simmer until the chili thickens and the flavors come together.
Boil the penne separately until just tender, then drain and fold it in.
Melt the shredded cheddar over the top before portioning into containers.

We buy salt 'to taste (15 g)' but the steps never say salt or season; the source seasons in step 2.
We buy pepper 'to taste (4 g)' but the steps never say pepper or season.

name: Beef Enchilada Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 8 cans (3066 g)
Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 3 cans (600 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (500 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (224 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
Corn Tortillas: 5, cut into triangles (440 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, then drain off the grease.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin and let them bloom in the hot beef for a minute.
Add the enchilada sauce and corn and simmer until it thickens up a bit.
Fold in the seasoned black beans and warm everything through.
Spoon it into bowls over the beans, then top with shredded cheddar so it melts in.
head_steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, then drain off the grease.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin and let them bloom in the hot beef for a minute.
Add the enchilada sauce and corn and simmer until it thickens up a bit.
Fold in the seasoned black beans and warm everything through.
Spoon it into bowls over the beans, then top with shredded cheddar so it melts in.

findings.detail: We buy '5, cut into triangles (440 g)' but no step uses tortillas; the source coats the tortilla triangles in the sauce in step 3 - this is the dish's enchilada component.
We buy '1/2 onion, diced (190 g)' but no step uses onion; the source browns it with the beef in step 2.
We buy 1/2 tsp garlic powder but no step uses it; the source adds it with the chili powder and cumin in step 2.
We buy 1 tbsp olive oil but no step uses it; the source heats it before browning the beef.
We buy salt 'to taste (18 g)' but the steps never say salt or season; the source seasons the beef in step 2.
We buy pepper 'to taste (4 g)' but the steps never say pepper or season.

name: Chinese Beef with Honey Black Pepper Sauce
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 5.25 tbsp (94 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain, then toss it with cornstarch and a splash of the soy sauce until every piece is lightly coated. Let it sit 15 minutes.
Start the rice.

Whisk the honey, oyster sauce, mirin, remaining soy sauce, and a heavy amount of coarse black pepper into a cup. Taste it. It should be aggressively sweet and aggressively peppery, because the beef and rice will tone it down.
Get a large skillet ripping hot and sear the beef in batches without moving it for the first minute. Pull each batch out just short of done.
Add the sliced onion to the pan and cook 2 to 3 minutes until it softens at the edges, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble hard until it thickens and turns glossy, which takes about a minute. Watch it closely, because honey sauces go from perfect to scorched fast.
Return the beef with its juices, toss to coat, and scatter the chopped peanuts over the top just before packing so they stay crunchy.
head_steps: Slice the beef thin and toss with cornstarch and soy sauce to velvet it.
Cook the rice and whisk honey, oyster sauce, mirin, soy sauce, and coarse black pepper into a sauce.
Sear the beef in batches in a very hot skillet and set aside.
Soften the onion, add garlic, then pour in the sauce and reduce until glossy.
Return the beef, toss to coat, and top with chopped peanuts.
Weigh rice and beef into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Step 2 says 'toss it with cornstarch and a splash of the soy sauce' but cornstarch is not in our list (the source uses no cornstarch at all).
We buy 1 tbsp salt but the steps never say salt or season.

name: Beef and Mushroom Stir-Fry Rice Plate
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.5 cups (168 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain and toss it with most of the cornstarch, a pinch of baking soda, some soy sauce, and a splash of water, then let it sit for at least fifteen minutes.
Cook the rice according to the package while the beef rests.
Stir the remaining cornstarch into a little cold water and mix it with the oyster sauce, the rest of the soy sauce, the beef broth, the chicken broth, sugar, and black pepper to make the sauce.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok until it smokes and sear the beef in batches in a single layer, just until browned, then set it aside. Do not cook it through, since it will finish in the sauce.
Add the butter to the pan and cook the mushrooms hard, without stirring much, until they release their water, it cooks off, and they brown.
Add the ginger, garlic, and the white parts of the green onions and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce mixture, bring it to a boil until it thickens and turns glossy, return the beef, add the sesame oil and the green onion tops, and toss to coat.
head_steps: Slice the beef thin and velvet it with cornstarch, baking soda, and soy sauce.
Cook the rice while the beef rests.
Mix oyster sauce, soy sauce, broths, sugar, and a cornstarch slurry into a sauce.
Sear the beef in batches in smoking hot oil, then set aside.
Brown the mushrooms in butter, then add ginger, garlic, and green onion whites.
Add the sauce, thicken, return the beef, finish with sesame oil, and portion over rice into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 0.5 tbsp salt but the steps never say salt or season; the source puts 1/2 tsp salt in the sauce mix.

name: Cuban Beef Picadillo Rice Bowls
ingredients: Salt (Morton): 1/8 to 1/2 tsp fine salt (6 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, green pepper, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, olives, and golden raisins.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes so the flavors come together.
Cook the rice while the picadillo simmers.
Spoon the beef over rice and serve.
head_steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, green pepper, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, olives, and golden raisins.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes so the flavors come together.
Cook the rice while the picadillo simmers.
Spoon the beef over rice and serve.

findings.detail: We buy '2 tablespoons, drained (36 g)' but no step uses capers; the source adds them to the tomato sauce mixture in step 3 as part of the dish's signature briny flavor.
We buy a jar of oregano but no step uses it; the source adds it with the cumin in step 3.
We buy 1 bay leaf but no step adds or removes it; the source simmers it in step 3 and removes it in step 5.
We buy salt but the steps never say salt or season; the source salts to taste at the end.
We buy 1/4 tsp pepper but the steps never say pepper or season.

name: Simple Beef Ragu Pasta
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, and Italian seasoning.
Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and rich.
Cook the penne until just tender, then toss it with the sauce.
Finish with a shower of parmesan over the top.
head_steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, and Italian seasoning.
Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and rich.
Cook the penne until just tender, then toss it with the sauce.
Finish with a shower of parmesan over the top.

findings.detail: We buy 1 tbsp vegetable oil but no step uses it; the source heats oil before browning the beef.
We buy 1 tsp sugar but no step uses it; the source stirs sugar in as an explicit finishing step.
We buy 1/2 tsp salt but the steps never say salt or season; the source salts the beef while browning.
We buy 1/4 tsp pepper but the steps never say pepper or season.

name: Beef Rendang Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Blend the onion, garlic, ginger, and jalapeno into a rough paste. Add a splash of water if the blender needs help moving.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wide heavy pot and fry the paste over medium heat until it darkens and smells sweet rather than raw, about 10 minutes. This is the single most important step, so do not shortcut it.
Stir in the lemongrass paste, turmeric, cinnamon, bay leaves, and black pepper and cook another minute.
Add the beef cut into large cubes and turn it in the paste until every piece is coated.
Pour in the coconut milk with the brown sugar and salt, bring it to a simmer, and cook uncovered on low for 2 to 3 hours. Stir every 20 minutes or so, more often near the end.

Keep going past the point where it looks done. The liquid will reduce, then break, then the beef starts frying in the coconut oil that separates out and everything turns deep brown. That is rendang, and it is a different dish from the milky stew it was an hour earlier.
Taste for salt and pull it off the heat while there is still a little gloss on the meat.
head_steps: Blend onion, garlic, ginger, and jalapeno into a spice paste.
Fry the paste in oil until darkened, then add lemongrass paste and dry spices.
Coat the cubed beef in the paste, then add coconut milk, brown sugar, and salt.
Simmer uncovered 2 to 3 hours, stirring often, until the liquid reduces and breaks.
Keep cooking until the beef fries in the separated oil and turns deep brown.
Weigh the pot and divide into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 4.25 cups dry rice for 'Rice Bowls' but no step ever cooks or combines the rice; the steps end at pulling the rendang off the heat.

name: Beijing Zha Jiang Mian Pork Noodles
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 35.25 oz dry (998 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the pork shoulder small, roughly pea-sized, so it eats like a sauce rather than a stew.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and cook the pork over medium-high heat until it browns and renders its fat.
Add the garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the green onions and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the hoisin sauce and soy sauce and let them fry in the fat for a minute, which is what takes the raw edge off.
Pour in the chicken broth, drop the heat to low, and simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and glossy and the pork is tender.
Boil the lo mein noodles to just tender, drain, and rinse briefly so they do not clump.
Cut the cucumber and carrots into matchsticks, then serve the sauce over the noodles with the raw vegetables and the green onion tops piled on.
head_steps: Dice the pork shoulder small and brown it in hot oil until the fat renders.
Add garlic, ginger, and green onion whites and cook until fragrant.
Fry the hoisin and soy sauce in the fat, then pour in the broth.
Simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and the pork is tender.
Boil the lo mein noodles and cut the cucumber and carrots into matchsticks.
Portion noodles into 14 containers, then top with sauce and raw vegetables.

findings.detail: We buy 0.25 oz (9 g) of bay leaves but no step uses them; the source infuses the oil with bay leaves, cinnamon, star anise, and Sichuan peppercorn before cooking the pork.
We buy 0.75 tbsp ground cinnamon but no step uses it; the source's cinnamon goes into the aromatic oil infusion our steps dropped.
We buy 0.75 tbsp sugar but no step uses it; the source adds sugar with the bean sauces.
We buy 1.5 tbsp black pepper but the steps never say pepper or season.
We buy 0.5 tbsp salt but the steps never say salt or season.

name: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 1.5 lb (700 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Drain the sauerkraut but do not rinse all the tang out of it. Core and shred the fresh cabbage, dice the onions, and slice the mushrooms.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot and brown the chicken thighs and the sliced smoked sausage until both have real color on them. Take them out and set them aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot until soft, then add the mushrooms and let them give up their water.
Stir in the sauerkraut, the shredded cabbage, the tomato sauce, the caraway seeds and the bay leaves.
Return the meat, add enough water to keep everything just submerged, and bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook low and slow for a couple of hours, stirring now and then. This is a stew that rewards patience, not heat.
Stir in the golden raisins near the end, season with salt and black pepper, and cook the rice separately to serve it over.
head_steps: Drain the sauerkraut, shred the fresh cabbage, dice the onions and slice the mushrooms.
Brown the chicken thighs and sliced smoked sausage in olive oil, then set them aside.
Cook the onions and mushrooms in the same pot until soft.
Add the sauerkraut, cabbage, tomato sauce, caraway and bay leaves, return the meat, and add water to just cover.
Simmer covered for a couple of hours, stir in the raisins, season, and serve over cooked rice.

findings.detail: Step 2 says 'slice the mushrooms' and step 4 says 'add the mushrooms and let them give up their water,' but no mushrooms are in our list (the source uses dried porcini).

name: Brazilian Galinhada (Chicken and Saffron Rice)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and season them with salt, black pepper and the lemon juice. Let them sit 20 minutes while you chop everything else.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high and brown the chicken in batches until it has real color on both sides. Do not rush this, because the fond on the bottom of the pot is the entire flavor base. Set the chicken aside.
Cook the diced onion and green bell pepper in the same pot for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and the tomato paste and cook 2 more minutes until the paste turns brick red.
Stir in the dry rice and toast it for 2 minutes so every grain gets coated in the tomato and the drippings.
Add the diced tomatoes, chicken broth and bay leaves, then nestle the chicken back in with all its juices and bring the pot to a boil.
Drop to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 20 to 25 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165F.
Scatter the frozen peas over the top, re-cover, and let it sit off the heat 10 minutes. Then pull the bay leaves, fluff from the bottom, and fold in the sliced green onions.
head_steps: Season the cut chicken with salt, pepper and lemon juice and rest 20 minutes.
Brown the chicken in oil in batches, then set aside and soften onion and bell pepper with garlic and tomato paste.
Toast the dry rice in the pot for 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, broth and bay leaves, return the chicken, cover, and cook on low 20 to 25 minutes.
Add peas off the heat for 10 minutes, fluff with green onions, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Step 2 says 'season them with salt, black pepper and the lemon juice' but neither salt nor black pepper is in our costed list, unlike every sibling card that buys them.

name: Buffalo Turkey and Potato Bowls
ingredients: Buffalo Wing Sauce (Frank's RedHot): 1 bottle (210 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (200 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): 1 tsp ground (8 g)
steps: Brown 6 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with a chopped yellow onion until no pink is left.
Bake the fries on sheet pans while the turkey cooks so nothing sits waiting.
Stir the buffalo wing sauce and shredded carrots into the turkey and let it simmer a few minutes.
Pile the buffalo turkey over the fries in each container.
Sprinkle the fat-free cheddar on top while everything is hot so it melts in.
head_steps: Brown 6 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with a chopped yellow onion until no pink is left.
Bake the fries on sheet pans while the turkey cooks so nothing sits waiting.
Stir the buffalo wing sauce and shredded carrots into the turkey and let it simmer a few minutes.
Pile the buffalo turkey over the fries in each container.
Sprinkle the fat-free cheddar on top while everything is hot so it melts in.

findings.detail: We buy 1 Tbsp garlic powder but no step uses it; the source stirs it in with the celery salt and pepper in step 3.
We buy 1 tsp celery salt but no step uses it; the source adds it in step 3 before the buffalo sauce.
We buy 1 tsp ground pepper but the steps never say pepper or season; the source adds it in step 3.

name: Cajun Chicken Etouffee Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the roux: heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium, whisk in the flour, and stir near-constantly for 10 to 15 minutes until it turns the color of peanut butter. Do not walk away; a burnt roux starts over.
Add the butter, diced onion, celery, and green bell pepper and cook 5 to 6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic for 1 minute more.
Gradually whisk in the chicken broth so the roux stays smooth, then add the Worcestershire, Cajun seasoning, thyme, bay leaves, and hot sauce.
Add the chicken thighs, cut into large bite-size pieces, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy thickens and the chicken reaches 165F. Pull the bay leaves and stir in most of the green onions.
Meanwhile, cook 3.75 cups dry rice with water per package directions.
Combine the rice and etouffee in your weighed pot, or portion rice first and ladle the etouffee over, your call. Finish with the remaining green onions.
head_steps: Stir oil and flour over medium heat 10 to 15 minutes into a peanut-butter-colored roux.
Cook the onion, celery, and bell pepper in the roux with butter, then add garlic.
Whisk in the broth gradually, then season with Worcestershire, Cajun seasoning, thyme, and hot sauce.
Add the chicken and simmer 25 to 30 minutes until thickened and 165F.
Cook the rice, combine with the etouffee and green onions, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 3.4 cans (1389 g) of diced tomatoes but no step uses them; the source adds the canned tomatoes with the Worcestershire and Creole seasoning in step 4 as the sauce's acidic component.
We buy 1 tbsp salt but the steps never say salt or season.
We buy 0.5 tbsp pepper but the steps never say pepper or season.

name: Cantonese Beef, Tomato and Egg over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, then scramble them in some of the vegetable oil over medium heat until just barely set and still soft. Pull them out early, since they will finish in the sauce.
Stir the cornstarch into a little cold water to make a smooth slurry and set it aside.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan and cook the ground beef with the garlic powder until browned with no pink remaining.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook them down until they collapse and the sauce turns thick and glossy.
Stir in the ketchup, sugar, soy sauce, and chicken broth and simmer for a few minutes so the flavors settle.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry while stirring and cook until the sauce thickens and turns shiny.
Fold the scrambled eggs back in gently so they stay in soft curds, and season with salt and black pepper to taste.
head_steps: Scramble the eggs in oil until just barely set, then set aside.
Whisk the cornstarch with cold water into a slurry.
Brown the ground beef with garlic powder.
Cook the diced tomatoes down until they collapse into sauce.
Add ketchup, sugar, soy sauce, and broth, then thicken with the slurry.
Fold the eggs back in gently, season, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 4.25 cups dry rice for a dish served 'over Rice' but no step ever cooks or combines the rice; the steps end at folding the eggs back in.

name: Cantonese Turkey Rice Bowls
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.75 cups (189 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide skillet over medium-high, add the ground turkey, and brown it, breaking it into fine crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the diced onion and minced garlic and cook 4 minutes until the onion softens and goes translucent.
Pour in the chicken broth, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and black pepper, and bring it to a simmer for 5 minutes so the flavors settle in together.
Whisk the cornstarch with a half cup of cold water until smooth. Cold water, always, since cornstarch in hot liquid turns into lumps you cannot whisk out.
Stir the slurry into the simmering pan and cook 2 minutes until the sauce turns glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Add the frozen peas and the sesame oil and cook 2 minutes more, just until the peas are hot and still bright green.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the gravy in its own pan for portioning.
head_steps: Brown the ground turkey in vegetable oil to 165F.
Add onion and garlic and cook 4 minutes.
Add chicken broth, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and pepper and simmer 5 minutes.
Whisk cornstarch with cold water and stir it in to thicken the gravy.
Add frozen peas and sesame oil and cook 2 minutes.
Cook the rice, portion by weight into 14 containers, and ladle the gravy over the top.

findings.detail: We buy 1 tbsp salt but the steps never say salt or season (the source relies on soy and oyster sauce for salt and lists none).

name: Carne Guisada (Tex-Mex Beef and Potato Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the sirloin into small cubes, pat them dry, and season with salt, black pepper, cumin, and oregano.
Brown the beef in the olive oil in batches over high heat until it takes on real color.
Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and diced jalapeno and cook until soft, scraping the pot bottom clean.
Sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for a minute so it toasts rather than tasting raw.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and the beef broth, along with the splash of soy sauce from the pantry list.
Cover and simmer low for 75 to 90 minutes, until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced into a gravy that clings.
Taste for salt and heat, then cook the rice separately.
head_steps: Cube and season the sirloin, then brown it in olive oil in batches.
Soften onion, garlic, and jalapeno in the pot.
Stir in the flour and cook a minute to toast it.
Add diced tomatoes and beef broth and simmer 75 to 90 minutes until thick.
Cook the rice and portion stew and rice into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 21.6 potatoes (4609 g) and the dish is titled 'Beef and Potato Stew', but no step ever adds potatoes; the source (isabeleats.com) contains no potatoes, so the steps track the source while the list added an ingredient the cook never uses.
Final step says 'then cook the rice separately' but rice is not in our costed ingredient list (source serves with tortillas/Mexican rice as a side suggestion only).

name: Cheeseburger Rice Bowls
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (180 g)
steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Stir in the beef broth, diced tomatoes, ketchup, dijon, and garlic.
Simmer until the sauce reduces and coats the beef.
Cook the rice separately, then stir it into the skillet or serve it underneath.
Melt the shredded cheddar over the top before portioning into containers.

Stir in the beef broth, diced tomatoes, ketchup, dijon, and garlic.
Simmer until the sauce reduces and coats the beef.
Cook the rice separately, then stir it into the skillet or serve it underneath.
Melt the shredded cheddar over the top before portioning into containers.

findings.detail: 1 Tbsp (50 g) Worcestershire is in the costed list but the five steps (brown beef, stir in broth/tomatoes/ketchup/dijon/garlic, simmer, rice, cheese) never mention it.
1 Tbsp (45 g) olive oil is costed but no step uses any oil; the beef is browned with no fat mentioned.
Salt (1 tsp) and black pepper (1/2 tsp) are costed but no step salts, peppers, or says 'season' anywhere.

name: Cheesy Taco Spaghetti
ingredients: Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 3.5 cans (992 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 7 oz (198 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until just shy of al dente, then drain, saving a cup of pasta water.
Meanwhile, brown the ground beef in your largest pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains; ground beef should hit 160F. Drain excess fat.
Add the garlic and diced jalapenos and cook 2 to 3 minutes, then stir in the taco seasoning and tomato paste.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Fold in the spaghetti with a splash of the reserved pasta water, then stir in the Mexican cheese blend until it melts into the sauce.
Top with the mozzarella, cover on low heat 3 to 4 minutes until melted, then finish with the sliced olives and chopped cilantro.
head_steps: Boil the spaghetti just shy of al dente and reserve a cup of pasta water.
Brown the beef to 160F, drain, then cook the garlic and jalapenos with taco seasoning and tomato paste.
Add the diced tomatoes and simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Fold in the spaghetti and melt in the Mexican cheese blend.
Top with mozzarella, olives, and cilantro, then portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Step 4 says 'Add the garlic and diced jalapenos' but no jalapenos are in the costed list; source (ohsweetbasil.com) uses no jalapenos either, so the step likely garbles the Ro-Tel green chilies that ARE bought.
0.5 tbsp black pepper is costed but no step uses pepper or says 'season' (salt is used in the pasta water only).

name: Cheesy Zucchini Beef and Rice Skillet
ingredients: Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (196 g)
Vegetable Oil (Great Value): 2 tbsp canola oil (40 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (2 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package. Set it aside to steam while you build the skillet.
Heat a large skillet over medium high heat with a little olive oil. Add the lean ground beef and brown it, breaking it apart as it cooks until there is no more pink.
Stir in the diced yellow onion and green bell peppers with a pinch of salt. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the diced zucchini, the taco seasoning, and the canned diced tomatoes with their juice. Stir it all together so the seasoning coats everything.
Let it simmer 5 to 7 minutes until the zucchini is tender. If it looks dry or starts to stick, splash in a quarter cup of water.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts into the mix. Serve over the cooked rice, or fold the rice right into the skillet.

Stir in the diced yellow onion and green bell peppers with a pinch of salt. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until they start to soften.

Turn off the heat and stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts into the mix. Serve over the cooked rice, or fold the rice right into the skillet.

findings.detail: 4 cloves garlic are costed but no step ever adds garlic; the source (confessionsofafitfoodie.com) contains no garlic at all, so it was added to the list but never wired into the method.
2 cups (720 g) beef broth are costed but never used; step 6 tells the cook to 'splash in a quarter cup of water' instead, and the source uses only water.
Step 3 says to heat 'a little olive oil' but the list buys vegetable/canola oil, not olive oil.
Black pepper 'to taste (2 g)' is costed but no step uses pepper or says 'season' (only a 'pinch of salt' in step 4).

name: Old-Fashioned Chicken and Dumplings
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.5 lb (2012 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and simmer them in the chicken broth with the onion, carrots, celery, bay leaves, salt, and pepper for about 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the broth tastes like something.
Pull the chicken out, shred it, and return it to the pot. Fish out the bay leaves.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little cold water and stir it into the simmering pot to thicken the broth slightly. Cold water first, always, or you get lumps you will never break up.

Make the dumpling dough by cutting the cold butter into the flour with baking powder and salt until it looks like coarse crumbs, then stirring in the milk just until it comes together. Overworking the dough makes tough dumplings, so stop mixing while it still looks shaggy.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the surface of the simmering pot, spacing them apart since they will swell.
Cover tightly and steam 15 minutes without lifting the lid. Every peek releases the steam that is actually cooking them.
Cook the rice separately and put a scoop in the bottom of each container to stretch the batch further.
head_steps: Simmer the chicken thighs in broth with onion, carrots, celery, and bay leaves for 30 minutes.
Shred the chicken back into the pot and thicken the broth with a cornstarch slurry.
Cut cold butter into flour with baking powder and salt, then stir in milk to make a shaggy dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the simmering pot, cover tightly, and steam 15 minutes.
Cook the rice and portion everything into 14 containers with dumplings divided evenly.

findings.detail: Final step says 'Cook the rice separately and put a scoop in the bottom of each container' but rice is not in the costed ingredient list.

name: Chicken Biryani Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1750 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the chicken breast into large bite-size chunks and marinate in the Greek yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and salt for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear; this keeps the biryani fluffy instead of gummy.
Melt the butter in your largest heavy pot over medium heat and cook the sliced onions 10 to 12 minutes until deep golden. Set a third of them aside for the top.
Add the marinated chicken with all its marinade, plus the cumin, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaves. Cook 5 to 6 minutes until the chicken firms up.
Add the rinsed rice, sliced jalapeno, most of the mint, salt, and the right amount of water for your rice (about 2 cups water per cup of dry rice, minus the marinade moisture). Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and simmer on the lowest heat 20 minutes, then rest off the heat, still covered, 10 minutes. No peeking; the steam is doing the work.
Check that the chicken reads 165F, pull the bay leaves, and fluff gently with a fork. Top with the reserved golden onions and remaining mint.
head_steps: Marinate the chicken chunks in yogurt, garlic, lemon, and spices at least 30 minutes.
Rinse the rice and brown the sliced onions in butter until deep golden.
Cook the marinated chicken with the whole spices 5 to 6 minutes.
Add rice, jalapeno, mint, and water, then cover and simmer on low 20 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, confirm 165F, fluff, top with golden onions, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: The list carries 'Milk (Fairlife): 0 tbsp (1 g)' - a vestige of the source's optional saffron-soaked-in-milk step - and no step ever uses milk.
0.5 tbsp black pepper is costed but no step uses pepper or says 'season' (the marinade and rice steps use salt only).

name: Chicken Jalfrezi
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2100 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 15 minutes and blend them smooth with a little of the soaking liquid.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite sized pieces and toss with turmeric, salt, and a spoonful of the white vinegar.
Start the rice.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet and sear the chicken hard until browned at the edges, then pull it out. It does not need to be cooked through yet.
Cook the sliced onions until golden, add the garlic and the blended chile paste, then the cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, garam masala, and chili powder and toast them for a minute.

Add the tomato paste and the canned tomatoes and simmer hard, uncovered, until the sauce thickens and darkens and the oil starts to separate, about 20 minutes. This reduction is the whole difference between jalfrezi and a watery tomato curry.
Return the chicken with the bell peppers and cook 6 to 8 minutes, just until the chicken is done and the peppers are still crisp. Finish with the rest of the vinegar and a big handful of cilantro.
head_steps: Soak and blend the dried chiles into a paste.
Toss the cut chicken with turmeric, salt, and vinegar, and start the rice.
Sear the chicken hard in a hot skillet and set aside.
Brown the onions, add garlic, chile paste, and dry spices, then the tomato paste and canned tomatoes.
Reduce the sauce about 20 minutes until thick and the oil separates.
Return the chicken with the peppers, cook 6 to 8 minutes, finish with vinegar and cilantro, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Step 6 toasts 'the cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, garam masala, and chili powder' but coriander is not in our costed list, even though it is 1 tsp of the source's (seasonsandsuppers.ca) core six-spice blend.
0.5 tbsp black pepper is costed but no step uses pepper or says 'season'.
